assertion_results.text: The response reports the AST07 status as declared-and-uncovered (or an equivalent 'not decidable from this package' status) and does not report the category as pass, clean, no findings, or an equivalent all-clear.
assertion_results.evidence: `declared-and-uncovered`; do not close the ticket on the basis of pinning alone.

assertion_results.text: The response explicitly declines to treat the declared sha256 content hash as evidence that no malicious update occurred, and supports that with a reason about authorship of the bytes or about an operator accepting a new hash.
assertion_results.evidence: The presence of a hash pin does not prove absence of compromise—it only prevents drift in the absence of operator action.

assertion_results.text: The response names all three AST07 attack scenarios — Malicious Update, Rollback Attack, and Hot-Reload Abuse — and states for each that a single point-in-time package cannot decide it.
assertion_results.evidence: (Malicious Update, Rollback Attack, Hot-Reload Abuse), meaning no static detector can confirm whether ...

assertion_results.text: For each of the three scenarios the response names at least one concrete piece of off-artifact evidence that would be required, such as a signed release-transparency or operator-held version-to-hash-to-publisher-key record, a resolver decision record paired with an operator-intent record, or host reload telemetry paired with directory ownership.
assertion_results.evidence: Response lists generic evidence (predecessor evidence, resolver decision records, reload telemetry) but does not assign a specific piece to each of the three scenarios.

assertion_results.text: The response does not tell the user the ticket can be closed on the strength of the pin.
assertion_results.evidence: do not close the ticket on the basis of pinning alone.
